analysis.title: Another year of resilience: 3 calls for the global economy in 2027
key_insights: ING's base call for 2027 is another year of resilient global growth, with inflation losing momentum and central banks keeping policy rates only mildly restrictive and largely on hold.

ING expects the US administration to avoid new trade tensions and new wars in 2027, while AI infrastructure investment slows somewhat but AI adoption and infrastructure spending support growth as energy prices return to more normal levels.
ING's risky call is that the transatlantic divide takes an unexpected turn. US midterm results may let US-Europe ties gradually recover, while Europe moves toward more political disruption.
Elections in 2027 in France, Italy, Poland and Spain, and possibly Germany, could strengthen eurosceptic forces, weigh on sentiment and investment and complicate European integration.

ING's bold call is global fiscal dominance: governments face higher interest rates, rising debt and investment needs while keeping social peace, which leads to spiralling government debt and higher rates.

ING sees two ways out of the fiscal squeeze. A globally coordinated debt restructuring is judged too bold even for this call. The second is pressure on major central banks to restart asset purchases and cap bond yields, with the option to write off government bonds held on central bank balance sheets.

macro_indicators.interpretation: ING's base case is a benign mix of modest growth and slowing inflation, with no numeric forecast given in this article.
Slowing inflation lets central banks hold policy rates, which ING describes as only mildly restrictive.
ING expects central banks to keep their powder dry rather than cut or hike aggressively.
Lower energy prices are one of the supports for growth in the base case.

risk_factors: European political disruption from eurosceptic gains in 2027 elections, weighing on sentiment, investment and integration.
Government debt spiral from higher interest rates, rising debt levels and investment needs.
Political pressure on major central banks to restart asset purchases and hold down bond yields, which could include writing off government bonds held by central banks.
An AI investment boom that slows more than expected.
The article notes a long list of potential downside risks and a lot of uncertainty and noise around the base case.
geopolitical: US midterm results may raise hopes of a gradual recovery in the strained transatlantic relationship.
Trump's second term ends in a lame-duck period in 2027, which ING expects to bring no new trade tensions or new wars.
Elections in France, Italy, Poland, Spain and possibly Germany in 2027 risk bringing stronger eurosceptic forces and political disruption in Europe.
External pressure from Washington had brought Europe closer together, and ING argues internal political divisions could now damage European unity.

tension_points.bull_case: ING's base call is resilient growth, easing inflation, steady central banks, no new US-driven trade tensions or wars, and support from AI adoption and infrastructure investment as energy prices normalise.
tension_points.bear_case: ING's risky and bold calls: European political disruption from 2027 elections, and global fiscal dominance in which governments pressure central banks to restart asset purchases to control bond yields.

theme_stances.key_argument: Governments under pressure from higher rates and rising debt may push major central banks to restart asset purchases to keep bond yields under control.
theme_stances.evidence: Our bold call for the global economy sees many governments struggling

theme_stances.key_argument: Elections across several European countries could strengthen eurosceptic forces and weigh on sentiment, investment and integration.
theme_stances.evidence: Europe risks ushering in a new period of political disruption

theme_stances.key_argument: Modest growth, slowing inflation and only mildly restrictive policy rates could produce an almost benign macro environment in 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: an almost benign macro environment could emerge in 2027
